title: Quiet weekend mode - ops crib (personal draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for a short internal comms push around a temporary "quiet weekend" mode we plan to run for a small window (experiment): reduced non-essential background jobs, tightened autoscale thresholds for non-prod fleets, and an ops-on-call posture tuned for faster handoffs. Not a public announcement yet — just a blunt, human-first crib I can share with the on-call buddies and a couple of PMs before we formalize a page.

Topline talking points (for a 2-minute all-hands blurb or manager heads-up):
- We’re running a controlled experiment this weekend to validate a reduced-cost, low-intervention ops posture for low-traffic windows.
- Core customer-facing inference endpoints stay fully supported (hosted API + dedicated). This affects only background jobs, nightly analytics jobs, and non-prod autoscale behavior.
- On-call remains staffed; escalation paths are unchanged. We’ll be tighter on paging thresholds for production errors.
- Objective: measure ops overhead reduction and ensure no measurable impact to latency/SLA for paid traffic.

Why we’re doing this (plain language):
- Traffic baseline shows a 65–80% drop in usage UTC 02:00–06:00 regionally; we want to see how far we can compress resource usage without increasing customer risk.
- Helps tune automated scale-down windows and informs batching/cache warmup strategies.
- Small, reversible experiment — we can abort within 20 minutes if we see regressions.

Quick FAQ / Anticipated questions + short answers:
Q: Will customer traffic be degraded?
A: No. We only alter non-customer-facing jobs and non-prod autoscale. Production model-serving pools remain at baseline for the experiment. If error rates for customer traffic increase, we abort automatically and re-warm.

Q: What if an on-call page fires?
A: Follow normal runbook. Pages for production SLO breaches are treated as highest priority. For non-prod/noise pages we will suppress lower-severity alerts to reduce distraction (suppression list below).

Q: How long does this run last?
A: Two nights: Saturday and Sunday UTC 02:00–06:00. Team agrees on a short dry-run the night before if needed.

Q: Can we roll this out to additional regions?
A: Not in this experiment — we limit to us-west-2 to keep blast radius small.

Operations checklist (pre-window):
- [ ] Update suppression list in PagerDuty (PD-suppress-quiet-weekend).
- [ ] Verify core production fleets pinned at baseline (runbook: fleet-check-v2).
- [ ] Notify Dedicated customers with reserved throughput > 2M tokens/day (email template below).
- [ ] Ensure 2x coverage for on-call: primary + floating buddy for escalation.
- [ ] Snapshot critical dashboards and enable 1-minute alerting for request error spikes.
- [ ] Confirm rollback automation (scale-up script + traffic-shift) is tested.

During-window quick ops script (to keep on phone):
- Check latency P50/P95 every 15m for prod routes.
- Look for KV-cache-miss spikes (index: cache:evaluations).
- If customer 5xx rate > 0.05% for 5m or P95 latency +30% over baseline: run emergency rollback (cmd: ops-rollback-quiet).

Suppressed alerts (examples):
- Non-prod CI job failures (job tags: ci/nightly/*).
- Analytics ETL partial failures flagged non-critical.
- Non-prod autoscale CPU threshold warnings.

Customer brief (short email for impacted Dedicated customers) — tone: transparent, optional opt-out.
Subject: Heads up — brief infra experiment this weekend (no expected impact)
Body: Hi — we’re running a short internal test this weekend to measure some low-traffic optimizations. Your production inference endpoints are unaffected and there’s no expected impact. If you’d like us to opt you out from any autoscale changes for this weekend, reply and we’ll lock your fleet. — Evan (on-call ops)

Internal all-hands micro-remarks (30–45s):
- Quick one: ops is running a small experiment this weekend to validate lower-cost posture during predictable low-traffic windows. Production serving is unaffected. On-call is fully staffed and ready to abort if anything looks off. Reach out if you want a quick walkthrough of the safety valves.

Handoff note for morning after (what to capture):
- Annotate any unexpected traffic blips + timestamps.
- Tag relevant traces with quiet-weekend:true for later aggregation.
- Short postmortem if we had to abort: timeline, root cause, and quick recommendations.

Edge cases I keep worrying about (personal):
- Sudden traffic from a partner integration that runs cron jobs in that window (double-check partner cron windows).
- Redis/KV cold starts when we scale back — measure recovery time and token cost.
- Latent background jobs that touch production DB during slower periods (watch for DB connection spikes after warm-up).

Notes to self / follow-ups to add to a formal doc:
- Add a clear chart: cost delta vs abort rate for 6 experiments.
- Write a short rubric for non-prod suppression categories (levels 0–3).
- Add a single-sentence opt-out flow for premium customers (ops console toggle).

Raw snippets / quick commands (save here):
- Emergency rollback: ./scripts/ops-rollback-quiet --region us-west-2
- Snapshot dashboards: ./tools/snapshot-metrics --days 7 --targets prod-routes
- Tagging traces: ./tools/tag-traces --key quiet-weekend:true --range last-24h

End notes (tone and next steps):
This doc is intentionally rough. Share with Priya and Marta, iterate into a tidy confluence page if the experiment passes. If we fail/abort, I’ll draft a short postmortem template and a sample customer note. If it’s clean, we iterate on automation to make 'quiet weekend' a scheduled option in the console for customers with low-traffic fleets.

-- Evan
